actions.action: Separate requested pickups from stock-backed confirmations
actions.mechanism: Treat expected returns as contingent supply; confirm only against inspected stock held for that pickup.
actions.implementation: Add requested, awaiting-return, confirmed, and recovery-required states. Atomically allocate an inspected item before confirmation; prevent allocation to overlapping reservations.
actions.check: Simulate delayed returns and simultaneous bookings. Every confirmation must retain a unique, inspected allocation; unsupported requests must remain visibly contingent.
actions.risk: Holding inspected items can reduce circulation; measure this tradeoff.

actions.mechanism: A threatening delay creates an owned recovery case, rather than silently leaving the pickup unchanged.
actions.implementation: On an overdue dependency, assign staff and a deadline. Offer inspected alternatives with condition and accessory differences through the supplied contact preference only.
actions.check: Test acceptance, rejection, and silence. Acceptance must atomically secure the alternative; otherwise retain an unresolved case and offer a revised window without implying confirmation.
actions.risk: Alternatives may disappear before acceptance; never interpret silence as consent.

actions.action: Inspect tools and detachable accessories separately
actions.mechanism: Component-level inspection can reveal usable combinations hidden by a whole-kit unavailable label.
actions.implementation: Track inspection and allocation per component. Assemble only manufacturer-compatible kits whose required parts passed inspection; obtain consent for any changed tool or accessory.
actions.check: Test a returned kit with one damaged accessory. Block the original configuration, prohibit shared-component double allocation, and release a rebuilt kit only after inspection and consent.
actions.risk: Compatibility errors can create unsafe kits; exclude uncertain combinations.

actions.action: Audit failures against a fixed request cohort
actions.mechanism: Keeping difficult requests in the denominator prevents cancellation from making pickup reliability appear better.
actions.implementation: Log each requested window before allocation. Retain library cancellations and delay-driven withdrawals; classify preventability from inspection, availability, consent, and contact timestamps.
actions.check: Report original-window unmet requests, prevented failures, and unknown cases alongside preventable failures. Canceling a difficult request must not improve any original-window fulfillment measure.
actions.risk: Missing evidence means unknown preventability, not an unavoidable failure.
